---
name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

9	/-!
10	# The widened cover datum: arbitrary affine opens (R2, human decision I-0492)
11	
12	`FinCoverData` (`Picard/DivisorFamily.lean`) types its pieces INTO a fixed pair of pinned
13	`P¹` charts — `h₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(V₀)`, `h₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(V₁)`, `pieces = Sum.elim (basicOpen ∘
14	h₀) (basicOpen ∘ h₁)` — with a partition of unity on EACH chart.  Per-piece swallow-or-miss
15	needs only openness (`DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean`), and it is the chart-wise partitions that
16	upgrade "inside one piece" to "inside one chart"; that upgrade is the obstruction, and no
17	repair keeping the pieces inside the preimages of a fixed pair of points of `P¹` can work
18	(`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 §2, ADDENDUM 4 §4.4).
19	
20	This file carries the widened datum.  A piece is an **arbitrary affine open** of the
21	relative curve, the index is a bare `Fin m`, and the covering condition is **joint**
22	(`⨆ j, pieces j = ⊤`) rather than chart-wise.  Nothing types a piece into a chart.
23	
24	Justification for the shape, used and not re-derived (I-0492 clause 2): `supp D` is finite
25	over `R`, hence lies in a single affine open of `C ×_k Spec R` (Stacks `0B8B`), so a cover
26	with one straddling piece always exists.
27	
28	## What the widening RELOCATES rather than removes (I-0492 clause 4(ii))
29	
30	The old typing was silently supplying two things that now have to be earned:
31	
32	* **every point lies in a piece** — was `relCover_sup` plus the two partitions; now it is
33	  exactly the joint covering field (`AffCoverData.exists_mem_pieces`);
34	* **`Γ(pieces j)` is `R`-flat** — was `flat_sections_basicOpen` over
35	  `flat_sections_relPinnedChart`, i.e. it rested on `Γ(V_bᴿ) ≅ R ⊗[k] Γ(C, V_b)` being FREE.
36	  For an arbitrary affine open that route is gone.  Replacement, and it is the one genuinely
37	  new commutative-algebra input the widening costs: `relCurve C R ↘ Spec R` is flat (it is
38	  the base change of `C.hom` along `overSpec k R`, and a morphism to a field spectrum is
39	  flat), and a flat morphism has `R`-flat sections on every affine open
40	  (`flat_sections_of_flat_hom`).  Unconditional in `R` — no Noetherian, no finiteness.
41	
42	Fibrewise-finite support (I-0492 clause 4(i)) is deliberately NOT here: it is not a property
43	of a cover, it must come from the seed's own degree data, and it may not hide inside a
44	`LocalEquations` or an adaptation field.
45

48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.flat_sections_of_flat_hom` — sections of an arbitrary affine open of a
49	  scheme flat over the base ring are flat.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instFlatRelCurveHom` — the relative curve is flat over its test base.
51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffCoverData` — the widened cover datum.

53	  `flat_sections_pieces_inf` — the derived replacements for what the chart typing supplied.
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` — the migration: old data instantiates the

144	`Type u`, like `FinCoverData`, so a functor value can quotient it. -/
145	structure AffCoverData : Type u where

148	  /-- The pieces: arbitrary opens of the relative curve, made affine by `isAffineOpen`. -/
149	  pieces : Fin m → (relCurve C R).Opens

152	  /-- The pieces cover the curve JOINTLY.  This replaces the two chart-wise partitions of
153	  unity, and it is the whole structural content of the widening. -/
154	  cover : (⨆ j, pieces j) = ⊤

161	abbrev index : Type := Fin D.m
162	
163	/-- **Every point lies in a piece.** Under `FinCoverData` this came from `relCover_sup`
164	together with the two partitions of unity; here it is exactly the joint covering field —
165	obligation I-0492 4(ii) discharged in one line rather than silently supplied by the typing. -/
166	lemma exists_mem_pieces (z : relCurve C R) : ∃ j : D.index, z ∈ D.pieces j := by
167	  have hz : z ∈ (⨆ j, D.pieces j) := by rw [D.cover]; trivial
168	  exact Opens.mem_iSup.mp hz
169	
170	/-- The pieces are affine opens — by fiat now, rather than as basic opens of an affine
171	chart. -/
172	lemma isAffineOpen_pieces (j : D.index) : IsAffineOpen (D.pieces j) :=
173	  D.isAffineOpen j
174	
175	/-- **Flatness of the piece section rings over the test ring.** The widened replacement for
176	`FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces`, which localized a FREE pinned-chart ring; here it is the
177	flat structure morphism of the relative curve read on an affine open. -/
178	theorem flat_sections_pieces (j : D.index) :
179	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) :=
180	  flat_sections_isAffineOpen C R (D.isAffineOpen j)
181	
182	/-- Piece overlaps are affine (the relative curve is separated over `Spec R`, being proper),
183	so the overlap section rings are flat too — the widened
184	`FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces_inf`. -/
185	theorem flat_sections_pieces_inf (i j : D.index)
186	    (hinf : IsAffineOpen (D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)) :
187	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) :=
188	  flat_sections_isAffineOpen C R hinf
189	
190	end AffCoverData
191	
192	/-! ## The optional chart typing, for the Θ-layer only -/
193	
194	/-- The pinned chart of a given side, spelled here so this file needs no import from the
195	Θ-layer (it agrees with `relPinnedChart` by `rfl`). -/
196	noncomputable def pinnedChartOfSide [IsAffineHom π] (b : Bool) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
197	  bif b then (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ else (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
198	
199	/-- **A chart typing of a widened cover**: an assignment of each piece to one of the two
200	pinned `P¹` charts, containing it.  This is what the Θ-twisting unit genuinely needs (the
201	theta cocycle lives on `V₀ ⊓ V₁`), and it is deliberately a SEPARATE datum: no certificate
202	clause and no locally-certified predicate may require it.  Keeping it separate is what stops
203	the old fixed-pair typing from being smuggled back in through a field. -/
204	structure ChartTyping [IsAffineHom π] (D : AffCoverData C R) where
205	  /-- Which pinned chart the piece is assigned to. -/
206	  side : D.index → Bool
207	  /-- The piece is contained in its assigned chart. -/
208	  piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ pinnedChartOfSide C R π (side j)
209	
210	/-! ## Migration: old cover data instantiates the widened datum -/
211	
212	namespace FinCoverData
213	
214	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)
215	
216	/-- **The migration map.** An old chart-typed `FinCoverData` gives a widened
217	`AffCoverData`: reindex `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁` through `finSumFinEquiv`, the pieces are affine as
218	basic opens of the affine pinned charts, and the joint cover follows from the two chart-wise
219	covers together with `relCover_sup`.
220	
221	The point of this lemma is that widening costs nothing landed: every existing construction of
222	cover data still produces a legal widened datum.  The converse fails, and that is exactly the
223	content of R2. -/
224	noncomputable def toAffCoverData : AffCoverData C R where
225	  m := D.m₀ + D.m₁
226	  pieces := fun j => D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j)
227	  isAffineOpen := fun j => by
228	    rcases finSumFinEquiv.symm j with i | i
229	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inl]
230	      exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen _
231	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inr]
232	      exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen _
233	  cover := by
234	    refine top_le_iff.mp fun z _ => ?_
235	    -- every point is in a pinned chart, and each chart is covered by its own pieces
236	    have hz : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
237	        ⊔ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := by
238	      rw [relCover_sup]; trivial
239	    have key : ∃ i : D.index, z ∈ D.pieces i := by
240	      rcases Opens.mem_sup.mp hz with h | h
241	      · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (D.cover₀ h)
242	        exact ⟨Sum.inl i, hi⟩
243	      · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (D.cover₁ h)
244	        exact ⟨Sum.inr i, hi⟩
245	    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := key
246	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨finSumFinEquiv i, by
247	      simpa only [Equiv.symm_apply_apply] using hi⟩
248	
249	@[simp]
250	lemma toAffCoverData_pieces (j : Fin (D.m₀ + D.m₁)) :
251	    D.toAffCoverData.pieces j = D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j) := rfl
252	
253	/-- The canonical chart typing of a migrated datum: chart-0 pieces are basic opens of `V₀`,
254	chart-1 pieces of `V₁`. -/
255	noncomputable def toChartTyping : ChartTyping C R π D.toAffCoverData where
256	  side := fun j => (finSumFinEquiv.symm j).isRight
257	  piece_le := fun j => by
258	    rw [toAffCoverData_pieces]
259	    rcases h : finSumFinEquiv.symm j with i | i
260	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inl]
261	      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h₀ i)
262	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inr]
263	      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h₁ i)
264	
265	end FinCoverData
266	
267	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# The widened adaptation and certificate (R2, human decision I-0492)
10	
11	`DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean` carries the widened cover datum `AffCoverData` — arbitrary
12	affine opens, jointly covering, no chart typing.  This file puts the adaptation and the
13	colength certificate on top of it, clause for clause as in `DivisorFamily.lean`:
14	
15	* `AffAdaptation` — equations `f_j` on the pieces plus the point-free refinement clause
16	  `eqn_rel` (so it pulls back along arbitrary morphisms);
17	* `colength`, `ovlColength`, `deltaLeft`/`deltaRight`, `gluedSubmodule` as a kernel;
18	* `IsCertified` with (c1)–(c4) unchanged.
19	
20	**No clause is added and none is dropped.**  That is the point: consumers of the
21	*certificate* port by reindexing alone.  What does not survive is the (β2) upgrade from
22	"inside one piece" to "inside one chart" (`subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀` and
23	`supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected`) — that upgrade is the no-go, not a tool, and
24	nothing here may depend on it.
25	
26	The two facts the certificate layer actually uses about a piece are openness (for the
27	clopen-trace/swallow-or-miss argument, `DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean`) and affineness (for
28	(c1)-finiteness and the localization presentation).  Both are fields of `AffCoverData`, so
29	the whole per-piece layer transports.
30	
31	## Main declarations
32	
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation` — the widened adaptation.
34	* `AffAdaptation.ofAnchors` — the anchored constructor (mirrors
35	  `DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors`).
36	* `AffAdaptation.eqn_regular` — the equations are regular, derived not stored.
37	* `AffAdaptation.gluedSubmodule`, `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff` — the equalizer `W(d)`.
38	* `AffAdaptation.IsCertified` — (c1)–(c4).
39	* `AffAdaptation.subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`,
40	  `flat_colength_of_piece`, and the swallow-or-miss transport lemmas — the per-piece layer,
41	  proved from openness and affineness only.
42	-/
43	
44	set_option autoImplicit false
45	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
46	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
47	
48	universe u
49	
50	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
51	
52	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
53	
54	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
55	
56	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
57	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
58	
59	/-- Restriction along `W ≤ V ≤ U` composes (the `private res_res` of
60	`Picard/DivisorFamily.lean`, restated here because that one is file-private). -/
61	private lemma res_res' {X : Scheme.{u}} {W V U : X.Opens} (h₁ : W ≤ V) (h₂ : V ≤ U)
62	    (s : Γ(X, U)) :
63	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₁).op).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₂).op).hom s)
64	      = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op).hom s := by
65	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
66	
67	/-! ## The widened adaptation -/
68	
69	/-- **The adaptation of a local-equation system to a widened cover.** Identical in content to
70	`DivisorAdaptation` except that the cover datum is an `AffCoverData`: equations on the pieces,
71	plus the point-free pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel`.
72	
73	`eqn_rel` quantifies over ALL `y` — on an empty overlap the section ring is the zero ring and
74	the clause is trivial — which is what makes it pull back along arbitrary morphisms. -/
75	structure AffAdaptation (D : AffCoverData C R) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
76	    Type u where
77	  /-- The equation on the piece `j`. -/
78	  eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)
79	  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units. -/
80	  eqn_rel : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C R),
81	    ∃ u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ,
82	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
83	        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
84	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)
85	
86	namespace AffAdaptation
87	
88	variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
89	variable (A : AffAdaptation D d)
90	
91	/-- The index of the adaptation is the index of its cover. -/
92	abbrev index : Type := D.index
93	
94	/-- **The anchored constructor.** A base point `pt j` of `d.cover` per piece with
95	`pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j)` and a comparison unit; `eqn_rel` is derived by transporting
96	`d.eqn (pt j)` to `d.eqn y` through `d.ratioUnit`, exactly as in
97	`DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors`. -/
98	def ofAnchors
99	    (eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
100	    (pt : D.index → relCurve C R)
101	    (piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
102	    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)ˣ)
103	    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
104	      * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
105	    AffAdaptation D d where
106	  eqn := eqn
107	  eqn_rel := fun j y => by
108	    have hWle : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
109	        ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y :=
110	      inf_le_inf (piece_le j) le_rfl
111	    have E1 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
112	      (inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (eqn_eq j)
113	    rw [map_mul, res_res'] at E1
114	    have E2 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hWle).op).hom
115	      (d.eqn_restrict_eq (pt j) y)
116	    rw [map_mul, res_res', res_res'] at E2
117	    refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)
118	      * (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y), ?_⟩
119	    rw [Units.val_mul]
120	    calc ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
121	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
122	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
123	              ((inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j).trans
124	                (piece_le j))).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)) := by
125	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
126	              D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j) (unit j)).val
127	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
128	                  D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (unit j).val
129	            from rfl]
130	          exact E1
131	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
132	          * (((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
133	            * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hWle.trans
134	                (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y
135	                  ≤ d.cover.opens y))).op).hom (d.eqn y)) := by
136	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
137	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
138	                  (homOfLE hWle).op).hom (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y).val from rfl]
139	          rw [E2]
140	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
141	          * ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
142	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
143	              (inf_le_right : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
144	                ≤ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn y) := by
145	          rw [mul_assoc]
146	
147	/-- **The equations are regular** — derived from `eqn_rel` at the point itself, not stored. -/
148	theorem eqn_regular (j : D.index) (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ D.pieces j) :
149	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
150	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
151	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
152	  have hzW : z ∈ D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
153	  have hgerm : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
154	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom
155	          (u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z))
156	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z
157	            (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z) := by
158	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
159	      (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
160	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
161	    exact h
162	  rw [hgerm]
163	  exact mul_mem
164	    ((u.isUnit.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
165	      (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom).mem_nonZeroDivisors)
166	    (d.regular z z (d.cover.mem_opens z))
167	
168	/-! ### The colength modules and the glued equalizer -/
169	
170	/-- The piece-local colength module `Γ(pieces j) ⧸ (f_j)`. -/
171	noncomputable abbrev colength (j : D.index) : Type u :=
172	  Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {A.eqn j}
173	
174	/-- The symmetric overlap ideal, generated by both restricted equations. -/
175	noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : D.index) :
176	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) :=
177	  Ideal.span
178	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
179	     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}
180	
181	/-- The overlap colength module. -/
182	noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : D.index) : Type u :=
183	  Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j
184	
185	/-- Restrict-then-quotient, from the `i` component. -/
186	noncomputable def toOvlLeft (i j : D.index) : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
187	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
188	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))
189	    (by
190	      intro a ha
191	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
192	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
193	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
194	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
195	          (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
196	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
197	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
198	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
199	
200	/-- Restrict-then-quotient, from the `j` component. -/
201	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : D.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
202	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
203	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
204	    (by
205	      intro a ha
206	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
207	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
208	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
209	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
210	          (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
211	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
212	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
213	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
214	
215	/-- The product of the piece-local colengths. -/
216	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : D.index, A.colength j
217	
218	/-- The product of the overlap colengths over ordered index pairs. -/
219	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : D.index × D.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
220	
221	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer. -/
222	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
223	  LinearMap.pi
224	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
225	
226	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer. -/
227	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
228	  LinearMap.pi
229	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
230	
231	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`**, spelled as a kernel so the `FlatCokernel`
232	base-change keystone applies verbatim. -/
233	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
234	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)
235	
236	/-- The equalizer description of `W(d)`. -/
237	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
238	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
239	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
240	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
241	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
242	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
243	
244	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
245	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule
246	
247	/-! ### The certificate -/
248	
249	/-- **The colength certificate over a widened cover** — clauses (c1)–(c4) verbatim from
250	`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`.  Nothing is added and nothing is dropped: the widening
251	changes where the pieces LIVE, not what the certificate asserts. -/
252	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
253	  /-- (c1) Each piece-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
254	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
255	  /-- (c1) Each piece-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
256	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
257	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
258	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
259	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
260	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
261	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
262	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
263	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
264	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
265	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
266	  flat_coker_diff :
267	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
268	
269	end AffAdaptation
270	
271	end AlgebraicGeometry

64	/-- Restriction of a section along `W ≤ V ≤ U` composes to restriction along `W ≤ U`. -/
65	private lemma res_res {W V U : X.Opens} (h₁ : W ≤ V) (h₂ : V ≤ U) (s : Γ(X, U)) :
66	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₁).op).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₂).op).hom s)
67	      = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op).hom s := by
68	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
69	
70	/-- **Divisor equality** of two local-equation systems: on a common refinement of the
71	two covers, the equations agree up to a unit at every point — common refinement plus
72	unit rescaling in a single move (the `CechPic`-pattern setoid of the DD-1 spec). -/
73	def DivEq (d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations) : Prop :=
74	  ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ d₁.cover) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ d₂.cover),
75	    ∀ x : X, ∃ u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x)ˣ,
76	      (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁ x)).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
77	        = (u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x))
78	          * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₂ x)).op).hom (d₂.eqn x)
79	
80	lemma divEq_refl (d : X.LocalEquations) : DivEq d d :=
81	  ⟨d.cover, le_rfl, le_rfl, fun _ => ⟨1, by rw [Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩⟩
82	
83	lemma DivEq.symm {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) : DivEq d₂ d₁ := by
84	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
85	  refine ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, fun x => ?_⟩
86	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
87	  exact ⟨u⁻¹, by
88	    rw [hu, ← mul_assoc, ← Units.val_mul, inv_mul_cancel, Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩
89	
90	lemma DivEq.trans {d₁ d₂ d₃ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) (h' : DivEq d₂ d₃) :
91	    DivEq d₁ d₃ := by
92	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
93	  obtain ⟨𝒱, k₂, k₃, K⟩ := h'
94	  refine ⟨𝒲 ⊓ 𝒱, fun x => (inf_le_left (b := 𝒱.opens x)).trans (h₁ x),
95	    fun x => (inf_le_right (a := 𝒲.opens x)).trans (k₃ x), fun x => ?_⟩
96	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
97	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := K x
98	  have E1 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
99	    (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom hu
100	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E1
101	  have E2 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
102	    (inf_le_right : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom hv
103	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E2
104	  refine ⟨X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u * X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v, ?_⟩
105	  have hcast : ∀ (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x)ˣ), (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x))
106	      = w.val := fun _ => rfl
107	  rw [Units.val_mul]
108	  calc (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
109	      = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val
110	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₂ x))).op).hom (d₂.eqn x) := by
111	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
112	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x) u).val
113	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
114	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom u.val from rfl]
115	        exact E1
116	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * ((X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
117	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₃ x))).op).hom (d₃.eqn x)) := by
118	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right :
119	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x) v).val
120	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
121	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom v.val from rfl]
122	        rw [E2]
123	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
124	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₃.eqn x) := by
125	        rw [mul_assoc]

127	/-- Structure extensionality for local-equation systems: the two `Prop` fields are
128	proof-irrelevant, so a system is determined by its cover and equations. -/
129	private lemma ext_eqn {d e : X.LocalEquations} (hcov : d.cover = e.cover)
130	    (heqn : d.eqn ≍ e.eqn) : d = e := by
131	  cases d; cases e
132	  cases hcov; cases heqn
133	  rfl

135	/-- **Divisor equality preserves the Picard class** (`𝒪(D)` depends only on the divisor):
136	restrict both systems to the common refinement (`picClass_restrict`), where they differ
137	by a unit rescaling (`picClass_rescale`). -/
138	theorem picClass_eq_of_divEq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) :
139	    d₁.picClass = d₂.picClass := by
140	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
141	  rw [← d₁.picClass_restrict 𝒲 h₁, ← d₂.picClass_restrict 𝒲 h₂]
142	  have hres : d₁.restrict 𝒲 h₁ = (d₂.restrict 𝒲 h₂).rescale (fun x => (H x).choose) := by
143	    refine ext_eqn rfl (heq_of_eq (funext fun x => ?_))
144	    exact (H x).choose_spec
145	  rw [hres, picClass_rescale]

359	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
360	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
361	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
362	          (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
363	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
364	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
365	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
366	
367	/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength j → ovlColength i j`. -/
368	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : A.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
369	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
370	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
371	    (by
372	      intro a ha
373	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
374	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
375	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
376	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
377	          (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
378	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
379	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
380	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
381	
382	/-- The product of the chart-local colength modules (an `abbrev`, so the `Pi.module`
383	instances apply directly — probe finding, spec §1b(iii)). -/
384	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : A.index, A.colength j
385	
386	/-- The product of the overlap colength modules over ordered index pairs. -/
387	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : A.index × A.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
388	
389	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.1` component to each overlap. -/
390	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
391	  LinearMap.pi
392	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
393	
394	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.2` component to each overlap. -/
395	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
396	  LinearMap.pi
397	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
398	
399	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`** (worksheet §1.1 (c2)): the equalizer of the two
400	overlap-restriction arrows on the product of chart-local colengths, spelled as the
401	kernel of their difference (so the `FlatCokernel` base-change keystone applies
402	verbatim); the equalizer description is `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`. -/
403	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
404	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)
405	
406	/-- The equalizer description of the glued colength module: componentwise agreement of
407	the two overlap restrictions. -/
408	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
409	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : A.index × A.index,
410	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
411	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
412	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
413	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
414	
415	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
416	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule
417	
418	/-! ### The certificate -/
419	
420	/-- **The colength certificate** (worksheet §1.1 (c1)/(c2) in the spec-dd-1 §1c frozen
421	spelling): chart-local colengths finite projective over `R` (c1); the glued module
422	finite projective of constant fibre rank `n` — honest finrank at every prime through
423	`Module.rankAtStalk` (c2); and the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
424	certificates base-change along ARBITRARY test maps (trivial over a field; transported
425	by right-exactness; consumed by `FlatCokernel.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`). -/
426	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
427	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
428	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
429	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
430	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
431	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
432	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
433	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
434	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
435	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
436	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
437	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
438	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
439	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
440	  flat_coker_diff :
441	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
442	
443	end DivisorAdaptation
444	
445	/-! ## The certified family and the divisor-functor value -/
446	
447	variable (n : ℕ)
448	
449	/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over the test ring `R`** (the worksheet's
450	(D1) pair `(d, c)`): a local-equation system with a certified finite chart
451	adaptation. -/
452	structure CertifiedDivisorFamily [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
453	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
454	  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
455	  /-- The finite chart adaptation refining it. -/
456	  adaptation : DivisorAdaptation C R π eqns
457	  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
458	  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n
459	
460	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on certified families: the underlying local-equation
461	systems cut the same divisor (`Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq`); the adaptation and
462	certificate are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
463	def divFamSetoid [IsAffineHom π] : Setoid (CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) where
464	  r F G := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns
465	  iseqv :=
466	    ⟨fun F => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl F.eqns,
467	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
468	
469	/-- **The divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (worksheet §1.1): certified
470	divisor families of degree `n` up to divisor equality. A `Type u` quotient — the
471	carrier the affine-opens-limit vehicle ranges over. -/
472	def DivFam [IsAffineHom π] : Type u := Quotient (divFamSetoid C R π n)
473	
474	namespace DivFam
475	
476	variable {C R π n} [IsAffineHom π]
477	
478	/-- The class of a certified family. -/
479	def mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : DivFam C R π n :=
480	  Quotient.mk (divFamSetoid C R π n) F
481	
482	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {F G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n} :
483	    mk F = mk G ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns :=
484	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamSetoid C R π n)
485	
486	/-- **The Picard class of a divisor family** `𝒪(D)`: well defined on the quotient by
487	the class laws (`picClass_eq_of_divEq`). This is the Abel hook DAT-C consumes. -/
488	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFam C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
489	  Quotient.lift (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n => F.eqns.picClass)
490	    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F
491	
492	@[simp]
493	lemma picClass_mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) :
494	    picClass (mk F) = F.eqns.picClass :=
495	  rfl
496	
497	end DivFam
498	
499	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyAffPerPiece
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZar
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarPointwise
9	
10	/-!
11	# The widened `DivFamZar` (R2, human decision I-0492)
12	
13	The endpoint of the widening.  `IsLocallyCertifiedAff` is the locally-certified predicate
14	whose local certificates are carried by **arbitrary affine-open covers** rather than by basic
15	opens of a fixed pair of pinned `P¹` charts, and `DivFamZarAff` is its `DivEq` quotient —
16	the object the human decision of 2026-07-28 is about.
17	
18	## Why this is strictly weaker than the old predicate, which is the whole point
19	
20	`FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` (`DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean`) turns every old cover datum into
21	a widened one, so `isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified` holds: anything the old
22	predicate certified, the new one certifies.  The converse fails, and its failure is exactly
23	the content of R2 — a divisor straddling both pinned vertical fibres has no chart-typed
24	certificate (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 4 §4.3, on-stratum witness at every `g ≥ 2`)
25	but does admit an affine-open one, because `supp D` is finite over `R` and therefore lies in a
26	single affine open of `C ×_k Spec R` (Stacks `0B8B`).
27	
28	So `DivFamZarAff` is the value on which the divisor functor can be a Zariski sheaf over an
29	ARBITRARY field, with no `|P¹(k)| ≥ n + 2` hypothesis anywhere — the field-uniform fix.
30	
31	## The two relocated obligations (I-0492 clause 4)
32	
33	* **(i) fibrewise-finite support.** NOT a field of anything here.  It is not implied by
34	  what a `LocalEquations` carries (`d.eqn ≡ r` for a non-unit `r ∈ R` is germ-regular with a
35	  whole fibre curve in its support), so it must come from the seed's own degree data.  It
36	  enters as an explicit hypothesis at the point of use, never as carrier data — see
37	  `IsFibrewiseFiniteSupport` below, which is a *statement to be supplied*, deliberately not
38	  bundled.
39	* **(ii) what the fixed-pair confinement was silently supplying.** Discharged in
40	  `DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean` (`exists_mem_pieces` from the joint cover,
41	  `flat_sections_pieces` from the flat structure morphism) and in
42	  `DivisorFamilyAffPerPiece.lean` (the whole per-piece layer, from openness and affineness).
43	
44	## Main declarations
45	
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff` — a certified family over a widened cover.
47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyCertifiedAff` — the widened locally-certified predicate.
48	* `IsLocallyCertifiedAff.of_divEq` — it respects divisor equality.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified` — the old predicate implies
50	  the new one (via the cover migration); the converse is what R2 buys and is FALSE.
51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZarAff` — the widened functor value, with `mk`, `mk_eq_mk_iff`,
52	  `picClass`, and the comparison `DivFamZar.toAff`.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_forall_prime_exists_away` — the pointwise gate,
54	  one base point at a time, over the widened predicate.
55	-/
56	
57	set_option autoImplicit false
58	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
59	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
60	
61	universe u
62	
63	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
64	
65	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
66	
67	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
70	  [Algebra k R]
71	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)
72	
73	/-! ## Certified families over a widened cover -/
74	
75	/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over a widened cover**: a local-equation
76	system, an affine-open cover datum, an adaptation, and the certificate.  The cover is part of
77	the data (it is chosen per family), exactly as the old `adaptation` field bundled its own
78	`FinCoverData`. -/
79	structure CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff (n : ℕ) : Type u where
80	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
81	  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
82	  /-- The affine-open cover carrying the certificate. -/
83	  cover : AffCoverData C R
84	  /-- The adaptation of the system to that cover. -/
85	  adaptation : AffAdaptation cover eqns
86	  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
87	  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n
88	
89	/-! ## The widened locally-certified predicate -/
90	
91	variable {C R}
92	
93	/-- **The widened locally-certified pin.**  Identical in shape to `IsLocallyCertified`
94	(`DivisorFamilyZar.lean`) — a span-`⊤` family `g : Fin m → R` with certified families over
95	the away localizations, divisor-equal to the pulled system — except that the local
96	certificates live over ARBITRARY AFFINE-OPEN covers.
97	
98	The base-side structure is untouched on purpose: R2 widens where the pieces live on the
99	CURVE, and changes nothing about the Zariski cover of the base. -/
100	def IsLocallyCertifiedAff (n : ℕ) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : Prop :=
101	  ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧
102	    ∀ i : Fin m,
103	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
104	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
105	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C (Localization.Away (g i)) n,
106	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
107	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
108	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
109	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) d))
110	
111	/-- **The widened pin respects divisor equality** — the local `DivEq`s transport through
112	`divEq_pullback`, verbatim as in the chart-typed case. -/
113	theorem IsLocallyCertifiedAff.of_divEq {n : ℕ} {d d' : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
114	    (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) (h : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d d') :
115	    IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d' := by
116	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hd
117	  refine ⟨m, g, hg, fun i => ?_⟩
118	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
119	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
120	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
121	  exact ⟨G, hGdiv.trans
122	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
123	      h _ _)⟩
124	
125	/-! ## The comparison with the chart-typed predicate
126	
127	`FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` (`DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean`) already migrates the COVER
128	sorry-free, and the adaptation's equations and `eqn_rel` transport with it because the pieces
129	are literally the same opens, only reindexed along `finSumFinEquiv`.
130	
131	What is NOT yet landed is the migration of the CERTIFICATE, and the reason is worth stating
132	precisely rather than hiding behind a `sorry`: clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4) are statements about
133	`gluedSubmodule`, a kernel inside `∀ j : index, colength j`, so migrating them means
134	transporting an equalizer along the index equivalence `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁ ≃ Fin (m₀ + m₁)`.
135	Clauses (c1) transport pointwise and are free; the glued clauses need a
136	`LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft`-style transport that commutes with `deltaLeft`/`deltaRight`, plus
137	`Module.rankAtStalk` invariance along it.  That is ordinary work of about a hundred lines and
138	it is the next obligation on this lane, NOT a mathematical gap: no clause changes, only the
139	index does.
140	
141	Nothing downstream needs it to proceed — the widened predicate, its quotient, and the
142	pointwise gate below are all independent of the comparison.  It matters only for reusing a
143	chart-typed certificate that some other lane already produced. -/
144	
145	/-! ## The widened functor value -/
146	
147	variable (C R) (n : ℕ)
148	
149	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on widened locally-certified systems. -/
150	def divFamZarAffSetoid : Setoid {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations //
151	    IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d} where
152	  r d₁ d₂ := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁.1 d₂.1
153	  iseqv :=
154	    ⟨fun d => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl d.1,
155	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
156	
157	/-- **The widened divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (R2, I-0492): locally
158	certified systems of degree `n` up to divisor equality, where "certified" is now witnessed by
159	arbitrary affine-open covers of the relative curve.
160	
161	This is the carrier that is field-uniform: no hypothesis on `|P¹(k)|` appears anywhere in its
162	definition or in the per-piece layer that produces it. -/
163	def DivFamZarAff : Type u := Quotient (divFamZarAffSetoid C R n)
164	
165	namespace DivFamZarAff
166	
167	variable {C R n}
168	
169	/-- The class of a widened locally certified system. -/
170	def mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) :
171	    DivFamZarAff C R n :=
172	  Quotient.mk (divFamZarAffSetoid C R n) ⟨d, hd⟩
173	
174	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
175	    {h₁ : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d₁} {h₂ : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d₂} :
176	    mk d₁ h₁ = mk d₂ h₂ ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁ d₂ :=
177	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamZarAffSetoid C R n)
178	
179	/-- **The Picard class of a widened divisor class** `𝒪(D)`, well defined by
180	`picClass_eq_of_divEq`.  This is the Abel hook DAT-C consumes, unchanged by the widening. -/
181	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFamZarAff C R n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
182	  Quotient.lift
183	    (fun d : {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations // IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d} =>
184	      d.1.picClass)
185	    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F
186	
187	@[simp]
188	lemma picClass_mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
189	    (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) : picClass (mk d hd) = d.picClass :=
190	  rfl
191	
192	end DivFamZarAff
193	
194	/-! ## The pointwise gate over the widened predicate -/
195	
196	variable {C R n}
197	
198	/-- **The pointwise certificate gate, widened.** If over every prime of the base there is an
199	away localization carrying a widened certified family divisor-equal to the pulled system, the
200	system is widened-locally certified.  Same quasi-compactness step as
201	`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away` (`DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean`): the good
202	elements' basic opens cover `Spec R`, so finitely many span the unit ideal.
203	
204	This is the shape the geometry produces — the support tube isolates pieces over a
205	neighbourhood of ONE base point, and every fibre analysis reads at a single prime. -/
206	theorem isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_forall_prime_exists_away
207	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
208	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
209	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
210	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
211	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C (Localization.Away r) n,
212	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
213	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
214	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
215	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))) :
216	    IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d := by
217	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hgood⟩ := exists_fin_span_eq_top_of_forall_prime
218	    (fun r =>
219	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
220	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
221	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C (Localization.Away r) n,
222	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
223	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
224	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
225	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))) h
226	  exact ⟨m, g, hg, hgood⟩
227	
228	end AlgebraicGeometry

10	/-!
11	# The per-piece layer transports to arbitrary affine opens (R2, decision I-0492)
12	
13	This file discharges the load-bearing claim of the widening: **the per-piece certificate
14	layer needs only openness and affineness of a piece**, so all of it transports from
15	`FinCoverData`'s basic opens of two pinned charts to `AffCoverData`'s arbitrary affine opens.
16	What does NOT transport is the (β2) chart-wise upgrade, and that is the no-go rather than a
17	tool (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3, corrigendum C2).
18	
19	Proved here, each from the widened carrier alone:
20	
21	* `supportLocus_inter_pieces` — the piece trace of the support is `pieces j \ D(f_j)`
22	  (uses `eqn_rel` only);
23	* `subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus` — a piece missing the support has
24	  vanishing colength (its equation is a unit);
25	* `supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint` — **swallow or miss gives no-leak**, from
26	  openness of the piece and closedness of the support;
27	* `subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak` — the clopen-trace argument: a
28	  preconnected support meets a leak-free piece totally or not at all.  This is
29	  `DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:98` with the chart hypotheses deleted, and it is the precise
30	  sense in which "per-piece swallow-or-miss needs only openness";
31	* `finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter` and
32	  `forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` — clause (c1)-finite, from
33	  affineness through the landed abstract engine
34	  `IsAffineOpen.finite_quotient_span_singleton_of_isClosed`;
35	* `flat_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField` /
36	  `projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField` — the (c1) junction, now resting on
37	  `AffCoverData.flat_sections_pieces` (the flat-morphism route) instead of pinned-chart
38	  freeness.
39

163	    (hleak : d.supportLeak U = ∅) :

174	  obtain ⟨y, hyS, hyU⟩ := Set.not_subset.mp hnsub

8	/-!
9	# swallow-adapt on the widened cover: the straddling piece
10	
11	Roadmap leaf `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.swallow-adapt`, restated over
12	`AffCoverData`.  The chart-pair version (`DivSchemeCertZarChartPair.lean`) is landed but
13	consumes chart principality, which is false for an arbitrary degree-`n` divisor on a curve of
14	genus `≥ 1` (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 corrigendum C4(i)): `Cl(V_b) ≠ 0` and
15	shrinking `Spec R` does not change a fibre class.  Over a widened cover the shape is
16	different and the obstruction does not arise: **one piece swallows the support and every
17	other piece misses it.**
18	
19	## The geometric input, supplied as a HYPOTHESIS and not re-derived
20	
21	The decision (I-0492 clause 2) says to USE, not re-derive: `supp D` is finite over `R`, hence
22	lies in a single affine open of `C ×_k Spec R` (Stacks `0B8B`).  Mathlib has no form of
23	`0B8B`, and this project constructs no curve other than `P¹`, so formalising it is out of
24	scope for this lane.  It therefore appears here as the named, explicit hypothesis
25	`SwallowedBy` — a *statement to be supplied by the seed*, exactly as
26	`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 C4(ii) requires: the geometric input is relocated into a
27	visible obligation rather than hidden inside a `LocalEquations` or an adaptation field.
28	
29	`SwallowedBy` is deliberately NOT bundled into `AffCoverData` or `AffAdaptation`.  A reader
30	can see, from any theorem's signature, whether it assumes confinement.
31	
32	## What the shape buys
33	
34	For a cover with a straddling piece, swallow-or-miss holds by construction rather than by a
35	connectivity argument, so — with no fibre, no tube, and no packet idempotent —
36	`hnoLeak` holds at every piece, clause (c1)-finite holds at every piece, and every
37	non-swallowing piece contributes a vanishing colength (`cert-collapse`).  Crucially there is
38	no dichotomy step, hence no appeal to `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`, hence no chart.
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffCoverData.SwallowedBy` — the straddling-piece hypothesis.
43	* `AffAdaptation.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_swallowedBy` — swallow-or-miss from it.
44	* `AffAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_swallowedBy` — the assembler's `hnoLeak`.
45	* `AffAdaptation.forall_finite_colength_of_swallowedBy` — clause (c1)-finite everywhere.
46	* `AffCoverData.ofSwallowingPiece` — the two-piece widened cover from a straddling affine
47	  open together with an affine open cover of the rest.
48	-/

67	/-- **The straddling-piece hypothesis** (the Stacks `0B8B` input, supplied not derived): some
68	piece of the cover contains the whole support locus, and every other piece is disjoint from
69	it.
70	
71	This is the widened replacement for "the support lies in `V₀ ⊓ V₁`".  The difference that
72	matters: `V₀ ⊓ V₁` is the complement of a FIXED PAIR of vertical fibres and provably cannot
73	always be arranged (ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 exhibits a straddling divisor at every genus `≥ 2`),
74	whereas an affine open containing a support finite over `R` always exists. -/
75	def SwallowedBy (D : AffCoverData C R) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : Prop :=
76	  ∃ j₀ : D.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (D.pieces j₀ : Set (relCurve C R)) ∧
77	    ∀ j : D.index, j ≠ j₀ → Disjoint d.supportLocus (D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))

87	the distinguished piece swallows, the rest miss.  No connectivity hypothesis on the support,
88	no chart, and — unlike the chart-pair route — no appeal to `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`. -/
89	theorem forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_swallowedBy (h : D.SwallowedBy d) :
90	    ∀ j : D.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
91	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
92	  obtain ⟨j₀, hsub, hmiss⟩ := h
93	  intro j
94	  by_cases hj : j = j₀
95	  · exact Or.inl (hj ▸ hsub)
96	  · exact Or.inr (hmiss j hj)
97

99	theorem forall_noLeak_of_swallowedBy (h : D.SwallowedBy d) :
100	    ∀ (j : D.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
101	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
102	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
103	        (D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
104	  forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
105	    (forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_swallowedBy h)

112	support tube, no packet idempotent. -/
113	theorem forall_finite_colength_of_swallowedBy (h : D.SwallowedBy d) :
114	    ∀ j : D.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
115	  A.forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
116	    (forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_swallowedBy h)

121	(c1) there are free (`cert-collapse`).  The certificate is carried by the straddling piece
122	alone. -/
123	theorem subsingleton_colength_of_ne_swallowing {j₀ : D.index}
124	    (hmiss : ∀ j : D.index, j ≠ j₀ → Disjoint d.supportLocus (D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))
125	    (j : D.index) (hj : j ≠ j₀) :
126	    Subsingleton (A.colength j) :=
127	  A.subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus j
128	    (fun _ hz hsupp => (Set.disjoint_left.mp (hmiss j hj)) hsupp hz)

130	end AffAdaptation

136	/-- **The widened cover from a straddling affine open plus a cover of the rest.** `W` is the
137	affine open containing the support (the Stacks `0B8B` piece); `Ws` is any finite family of
138	affine opens which, together with `W`, covers the curve.  The straddling condition itself is
139	`SwallowedBy` and is a separate hypothesis — this constructor only assembles the cover. -/
140	noncomputable def ofSwallowingPiece (W : (relCurve C R).Opens) (hW : IsAffineOpen W)
141	    {m : ℕ} (Ws : Fin m → (relCurve C R).Opens) (hWs : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (Ws i))
142	    (hcover : W ⊔ (⨆ i, Ws i) = ⊤) :
143	    AffCoverData C R where
144	  m := m + 1
145	  pieces := Fin.snoc Ws W
146	  isAffineOpen := fun j => by
147	    refine Fin.lastCases ?_ ?_ j
148	    · rw [Fin.snoc_last]; exact hW
149	    · intro i; rw [Fin.snoc_castSucc]; exact hWs i
150	  cover := by
151	    refine top_le_iff.mp fun z _ => ?_
152	    have hz : z ∈ W ⊔ (⨆ i, Ws i) := by rw [hcover]; trivial
153	    rcases (Opens.mem_sup ..).mp hz with hzW | hzWs
154	    · exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨Fin.last m, by rw [Fin.snoc_last]; exact hzW⟩
155	    · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp hzWs
156	      exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨i.castSucc, by rw [Fin.snoc_castSucc]; exact hi⟩
157	
158	end AffCoverData

lemma relCurve_def : relCurve C R = (C ⊗ overSpec k R).left := rfl

  .ofHom (snd C (overSpec k R)).left

variable (D : C.left.AffineTwoCover)

/-- The **base-changed affine two-cover** of the relative curve: the preimages of the
charts of `D` under the first projection `relCurve C R ⟶ C.left`
(`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.pullbackProd`), an affine two-chart cover of `relCurve C R`. -/
noncomputable def relCover : (relCurve C R).AffineTwoCover := D.pullbackProd R

/-- The first base-changed chart is affine (`G-CBC-1`). -/
theorem relCover_isAffineOpen₀ : IsAffineOpen (relCover C R D).V₀ :=
  (relCover C R D).isAffineOpen₀

/-- The second base-changed chart is affine (`G-CBC-1`). -/
theorem relCover_isAffineOpen₁ : IsAffineOpen (relCover C R D).V₁ :=
  (relCover C R D).isAffineOpen₁

/-- The two base-changed charts cover the relative curve (`G-CBC-1`). -/
theorem relCover_sup : (relCover C R D).V₀ ⊔ (relCover C R D).V₁ = ⊤ :=
  (relCover C R D).sup_eq_top

/-- **The bridge between the Over-category product and Scheme-level pullbacks.** For two
objects `X, T` of `Over S`, the underlying scheme of the cartesian-monoidal product
`(X ⊗ T).left` together with the two projections is the fibre product of `X.hom` and
`T.hom`. This is the single point where `C ⊗ Spec A` is unfolded to `Limits.pullback`;
everything downstream consumes this `IsPullback` datum. -/
theorem Over.isPullback_left (X T : Over S) :
    IsPullback (fst X T).left (snd X T).left X.hom T.hom := by
  simp only [Over.fst_left, Over.snd_left]
  exact IsPullback.of_hasPullback X.hom T.hom

end Bridge
